The test image shows a corn leaf with a single, round, white/cream-colored spot with slightly diffuse edges. This is a leaf symptom. Let me check my top candidates.

Top candidates based on appearance: Eyespot (circular spots), Holcus_Spot (circular white/tan spots), and possibly others. Let me view references one at a time.
Eyespot shows many small spots with rings/halos - very different from the single large white spot in the test image. Let me check Holcus_Spot.
Very strong visual match! Holcus_Spot shows a single round white/pinkish spot on a green leaf, very similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates to be thorough.
Common_Smut shows large galls/growths distorting the leaf - completely different. Let me check Southern_Rust and Tar_Spot.
Southern_Rust shows small scattered pustules - not matching. Let me check more candidates.
Tar_Spot shows black raised spots - not matching. Let me check Carbonum_Leaf_Spot and Northern_Leaf_Blight.
Carbonum_Leaf_Spot shows many small tan/brown lesions - not matching. Let me check Gray_Leaf_Spot and Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight.
Gray_Leaf_Spot shows rectangular lesions bounded by veins - not matching. Now let me view a second Holcus_Spot reference to confirm the match.

This second Holcus_Spot reference also shows round, white/tan spots on the leaf, consistent with the test image. The test image's single round white/cream spot with papery texture on an otherwise green corn leaf matches Holcus_Spot very well.

Key evidence:
- Single round/oval white-to-tan spot on a green corn leaf
- Papery, light-colored center
- Spot size consistent with Holcus_Spot (1/8 to 1/4 inch range, close-up photo)
- No rings/halos ruling out Eyespot; no dark raised structures ruling out Tar_Spot; no pustules ruling out rusts; no rectangular shape ruling out Gray_Leaf_Spot

All 8 views used across 8 different classes: Eyespot, Holcus_Spot (x2), Common_Smut, Southern_Rust, Tar_Spot, Carbonum_Leaf_Spot, Gray_Leaf_Spot.
